content.text:
I fixed the misspelling and committed it as one commit, `f6299fd`, so `git revert f6299fd` undoes it in one go.

- **What changed:** each of the three files (`data/2025-10.csv`, `2025-11.csv`, `2025-12.csv`) had one `wholsale` row, now `wholesale`. That's 3 lines in total.
- **Check:** `scripts/check.sh` printed OK. This time it did cover the edited files, because they're all 2025 files.
- **Nothing left to fix:** `wholsale` no longer appears in any tracked file. `out/summary.csv` didn't contain it, so it doesn't need regenerating.
- **Inbox copy:** `inbox/2025-12.csv` still has the misspelling. Git doesn't track it, so the commit can't include it. If you fix it there too, a revert won't undo that part.
- **Commit message:** the project wants messages to start with the data month, but this commit spans three months. I used `2025-10, 2025-11, 2025-12: …`, which may not group cleanly in the import log. If you'd rather it filed under one month, I can reword it.

January is still uncommitted and unchanged.
